subjects.displayTitle: Prayer for healing: body, spirit, and the reach of mercy
subjects.introduction: Thy name is my healing, Bahá’u’lláh teaches the sick to say, and remembrance of Thee is my remedy. Illness shrinks the world to one aching place, and the prayers for healing answer it with the largest images there are: an ocean of divine favour, rains of mercy from the clouds of grace, the robe of well-being. They ask plainly for the body to be made whole, and in the same breath for tranquillity, patience and the strength to rise and serve. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that such prayers reach both body and spirit, and that a death after many supplications is no verdict on anyone’s faith. Physicians who unite the medicine of bodies with the medicine of souls are prayed for by name, much as Sirach honours the doctor’s skill while urging the sick person to pray [1]. Each plea, for a child, for a handmaiden, for oneself, widens into a prayer for the whole afflicted world. The way leads on toward health and healing in its material and spiritual forms and to the divine Physician.
subjects.arc: Begin with healing as relationship, hold bodily care and uncertainty together, and widen the prayer toward service and the world.

order.why: Open with the intimate language of remembrance and healing.
Establish the bodily and spiritual scope and qualified answer.
Give physicians and their work a central place.
Hear grief asking for the physician’s compassionate attention.
shortened: O beloved physician! If thou art indeed a skilled and able healer, prescribe a healing medicine, for I am ailing; administer a soothing remedy, for I am sorely afflicted. Bring peace and tranquillity to my bereaved soul, and relieve the burning grief that consumeth my being. Lay a balm upon my wounded heart, and shed a sprinkling of healing waters upon my inflamed limbs and organs.

order.why: Allow a brief direct cry for balm.
Continue with concrete wounds and salve.
Hear a prayer from the limits of available treatment.
shortened: O Lord! The skill of physicians has failed to treat me and the expertise of healers and doctors is bewildered by my ailments. You are the healing of my illness and the cooling of my burning and the quenching of my thirst. Have mercy upon me through Your grace and generosity.

order.why: Acknowledge death despite prayer without blaming the sufferer.
Read hope within the language of an appointed time.
shortened: We beseech God to heal thee and cure thee of thy ailment and illness. Verily, He is the Answerer of the prayers of the suppliants. When the appointed time cometh, He will cause the rains of mercy and healing to descend upon thee from the clouds of His grace.

order.why: Place tranquillity and constancy beside restored health.
shortened: Send down, then, upon him Thy healing, and make him whole, and endue him with a constancy vouchsafed by Thee, and a tranquillity bestowed by Thy highness.

order.why: Consider joy and spiritual strength amid bodily weakness.
shortened: If I am sick, I gain eternal health.

O Thou Lord of the Kingdom! Cause Thou the rejoicing of my heart; empower my weak spirit and strengthen my exhausted nerves. Illumine Thou my eyes: suffer my ears to become hearing, so that I may hearken to the music of the Kingdom and attain to the joy and happiness everlasting.

order.why: Hear the invitation to sincere supplication during trial.
shortened: I supplicate God to alleviate thy trials and look upon thee with the eye of His mercy under all aspects.

Turn thou to the Kingdom of thy great Lord with a truthful heart and with all devotion, sincerity and great spirituality and ask to be healed from pain and passions and be confident in the great bounty of thy Lord.

order.why: Explore remembrance as balm for the heart.
Connect recognition and love with the imagery of healing.
Bring patience and forgiveness into the petition.
Keep the short contrast between need and divine shelter.
A concise supplication for healing, assistance and guidance.
Turn from poverty and illness toward gracious provision.
shortened: I am but a poor creature, O my Lord; I have clung to the hem of Thy riches. I am sore sick; I have held fast the cord of Thy healing. Deliver me from the ills that have encircled me, and wash me thoroughly with the waters of Thy graciousness and mercy, and attire me with the raiment of wholesomeness, through Thy forgiveness and bounty.

order.why: Introduce the cleansing waters of mercy.
shortened: O God, my God! I beg of Thee by the ocean of Thy healing, and by the splendors of the Day-Star of Thy grace, and by Thy Name through which Thou didst subdue Thy servants, and by the pervasive power of Thy most exalted Word and the potency of Thy most august Pen, and by Thy mercy that hath preceded the creation of all who are in heaven and on earth, to purge me with the waters of Thy bounty from every affliction and disorder, and from all weakness and feebleness.

order.why: Read the related healing formula in its own source.
shortened: "O my God, my God! I beseech Thee by the ocean of Thy healing, and by the splendors of the Day-Star of Thy grace, and by Thy Name through which Thou didst subdue Thy servants, and by the penetrating power of Thy most exalted Word and Thy most august Pen, and by Thy mercy that hath preceded the creation of all who are in heaven and on earth, to purify me with the waters of Thy bounty from every affliction and disorder, and from all weakness and feebleness.

order.why: Continue through the named fountains of grace.
shortened: O my Lord! Give me to drink from the Kawthar of Thy favor and the Tasnim of Thy grace and bounty, that it may purify me from all that Thy good-pleasure abhorreth and deliver me from this malady that hath seized me, for Thou hast ever been the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful unto Thy servants.

order.why: Widen water into an ocean of healing.
Move through rain, ocean, heaven and sun.
Read light and mercy beside the request for healing.
Hear bodily weakness asking for an antidote.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the ocean of Thy grace and by that which lieth concealed therein of the pearls of Thy knowledge and wisdom, to ordain for me through Thy Most Exalted Pen that which shall be a healing for ailments and an antidote for bodily weakness.

order.why: Add protection and strength.
shortened: I entreat Thee by Thy name whereby Thou hast subjected all created things, both visible and invisible, and through which the breath that is life indeed was wafted over the entire creation, to strengthen me by Thy power which hath encompassed the heavens and the earth, and to guard me from all sickness and tribulation.

order.why: Retain the direct acknowledgment of an inner and outer malady.
shortened: Say: Glory be to Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by this Name through which Thou hast shattered the idols of fancy and desire, and through which Thou hast become independent of all who dwell in the kingdom of glory and eternity, to send down upon me from the clouds of Thy mercy that which will purify me from this malady that hath troubled my inner and outer being.

order.why: Connect protection with readiness to serve.
shortened: O my Lord! Thou seest me gazing toward the heaven of Thy grace and beseeching the outpourings of Thy mercy and awaiting the streams of Thy loving-kindness and favors. I beseech Thee by Thy power that hath encompassed all created things to preserve me through the hosts of the unseen and the seen and to ordain for me that which will purify me from every disease and illness and disturbance.
O my Lord! Thou seest him who is related to Thy Self standing ready to serve Thee - send down upon him from the heaven of Thy mercy the rains of Thy healing.

order.why: Make removal of hindrances serve nearness and action.
shortened: My God, my God! Thou seest me turning toward Thee, speaking Thy praise, and standing to serve Thy Cause amidst the enemies of Thy Self. I beseech Thee by the oceans of Thy grace, the ships of Thy power, and the lights of Thy countenance, to ordain for me that which shall profit me in all the worlds of Thy worlds. Then I beseech Thee by Thy Name the Healer, by Thy Name the Sufficient, and by Thy Name the Helper, to purify me from every disease and malady and from all that hindereth me from drawing nigh unto Thee and arising to serve in Thy days.

order.why: Carry recovery toward gratitude and service.
Turn the petitioner into a servant of others’ healing.
shortened: O my God! Aid this broken one who is humbled at Thy sublime threshold to revive spirits, heal bodies, spread Thy traces among all beings, and exalt the word of piety through the power of guidance.

order.why: Hear encouragement addressed to a spiritual physician.
Attend to the vulnerability of a suckling child.
Place children and sick people within shared care.
shortened: Give the thirsty to drink from the Salsabil of grace and make the poor rich from the treasure of the Kingdom. Nurture the children in the cradle of grace until they reach maturity. Heal the sick with heavenly medicine that they may find health and well-being.

order.why: Retain a prayer for the well-being of two people.
Read the sustained petition for a sick handmaiden.
shortened: She is sick, O my God, and hath entered beneath the shadow of the Tree of Thy healing; afflicted, and hath fled to the City of Thy protection; diseased, and hath sought the Fountain-Head of Thy favors; sorely vexed, and hath hasted to attain the Well-Spring of Thy tranquillity; burdened with sin, and hath set her face toward the court of Thy forgiveness.

Attire her, by Thy sovereignty and Thy loving-kindness, O my God and my Beloved, with the raiment of Thy balm and Thy healing, and make her quaff of the cup of Thy mercy and Thy favors. Protect her, moreover, from every affliction and ailment, from all pain and sickness, and from whatsoever may be abhorrent unto Thee.

order.why: Keep the brief personal appeal beside it.
shortened: O my Most Merciful Lord, your sick handmaiden yearn your great grace and resplendent healing. Thou art the Ever-Forgiving, the Merciful.

order.why: Continue the request for mercy and well-being.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the Light whereby the horizon of the heaven of Thy bounty was illumined, to send down upon this handmaiden of Thine mercy and healing through Thy generosity and grace.
O Lord! Purify her from ailments and grant her well-being.

order.why: Bring tender compassion to hardship.
Show a request carried on another person’s behalf.
shortened: Thou seest one of Thy maidservants who desireth from this Thy servant that which Thou wouldst make a healing for her through Thy grace, and health from Thy presence, and well-being from Thy side.

Then I beseech Thee by Thy Beloved One, through Whose advent the celestial spheres were honored, to send down upon her from the heaven of Thy healing that which will gladden the hearts of Thy servants and Thy handmaidens.

order.why: Hear urgency when patience has become exhausted.
Keep the plea for someone overtaken by sickness.
Attend to weakness and being confined to bed.
Connect healing with restoring what feels scattered.
Preserve the Báb’s particular prayer concerning an inflamed eye.
Place bodily sight beside inward perception.
shortened: O Lord, heal the eyes of Thy servant and illumine his insight to behold the signs of Thy holiness, and cause him to hear the melodies of the birds of praise in the garden of divine unity through Thy grace and bounty, and make him pure and sincere for Thy gracious countenance. Verily, Thou art the Merciful.

order.why: Retain the particular instruction in its recorded context.
Read seen and unseen disease together.
Keep the historically situated petition amid opposition.
shortened: This servant, submissive and humble before Thy exalted Threshold, calls upon Thee, supplicating and imploring before Thy Most Great Mercy, taking refuge in the cave of Thy protection and most mighty safekeeping, that Thou wouldst protect him from the evil of enemies and make his word supreme and the word of his foes and adversaries abased, and heal him from his ailments which have weakened his strength and the maladies that have afflicted him with great force.

order.why: Connect protection from oppression with protection from illness.
Widen the petition to a community of afflicted people.
Bring thirst and weakness together.
shortened: Have mercy, O Lord, on the feeble, make whole the sick, and quench the burning thirst.

order.why: Let the prayer reach poverty, fear and guidance.
shortened: Illumine the hearts, make the eyes seeing, make the ears hearing. Bring the dead to life, heal the sick, make the poor wealthy, grant security to those who are afraid, accept us in Your Kingdom, and enlighten us with the light of guidance.

order.why: Preserve the petition for servants to fulfill divine commands.
Extend protection to the loved ones collectively.
Carry hope toward the Most Glorious Kingdom.
shortened: O Lord! He is sick and seeks healing, hungry and craves Thy bounties and favors, thirsty and seeks refreshment, and love-smitten yearning for the wine of meeting Thee. Ordain for him every good in the Most Glorious Kingdom, mention him in the Supreme Concourse, and grant him a true and lofty tongue.

order.why: Gather the recurring petitions in the Long Healing Prayer.
shortened: He is the Healer, the Sufficer, the Helper, the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful.

And again do I beseech Thee, by these most beauteous names, by these most noble and sublime attributes, and by Thy most Exalted Remembrance, and by Thy pure and spotless Beauty, and by Thy hidden Light in the most hidden pavilion, and by Thy Name, cloaked with the garment of affliction every morn and eve, to protect the bearer of this blessed Tablet, and whoso reciteth it, and whoso cometh upon it, and whoso passeth around the house wherein it is.  Heal Thou, then, by it every sick, diseased and poor one, from every tribulation and distress, from every loathsome affliction and sorrow, and guide Thou by it whosoever desireth to enter upon the paths of Thy guidance, and the ways of Thy forgiveness and grace.

order.why: Close by asking for the healing of the world.

questions: What different meanings of healing emerge as you move between bodily relief, tranquillity, insight, and service?
How might a community pray with hope while accompanying someone whose illness continues?
What does the prayer for physicians suggest about the relationship between spiritual care and practical skill?
How do the images of water, shelter, rain, and light shape the experience of vulnerability?
How does Sirach’s account of prayer and medical knowledge illuminate the comparison, and what belongs to its own religious setting?
What changes when the prayer moves from one person’s pain to the healing of the world?

references.label: 1 · Sirach 38:1–14 · Prayer and the physician
references.note: Sirach honors the physician’s knowledge and the medicines of the earth while urging the sick person to pray; the physician also prays for sound diagnosis and treatment. Compare this joining of practical care and dependence on God with the prayer for physicians in this compilation. Sirach’s language of purification and offerings belongs to its own religious setting. The passage offers a comparison in care, not a diagnosis or a promise about a particular illness.

subjects.displayTitle: Government and people: reciprocal trust and the common good
subjects.introduction: The progress of a nation depends on the strength of its government, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes, and the strength of a government depends on the prosperity of its nation; the two are twins. That reciprocity is the heart of the subject. Where a ruler’s justice, the skill of administrators and the effort of the people combine, their relationship is as sweet as milk and honey. But trust is not left to sentiment. He calls for a treaty between government and people with the rights of each fixed so that neither may transgress, for constitutional arrangements, accountable ministers, elections resting on public confidence, equal justice and equal opportunity, and for rulers who remember that their judgments will be weighed by a divine Judge. Much of this was written amid Iran’s upheavals and foreign intervention, and its warnings against faction and bloodshed belong to that history. Confucius, asked what a state could do without, surrendered arms and even food before the confidence of the people [1], a priority that sharpens the question of how authority earns trust. From here the way leads to constitutional government, to obedience and respect for authority, to elections, and to the meaning of true liberty.
subjects.arc: Start with mutual dependence, examine rights and accountability, then read historical conflict through the demands of justice and reconciliation.

order.why: Sets out reciprocal responsibilities of government and people.
Open with the cooperation of ruler, officials and people.
Make their prosperity explicitly interdependent.
Place justice and sound laws beside obedience.
Introduce specified rights and limits on transgression.
shortened: Therefore, a treaty must be executed between government and people, with the rights of both sides fixed, preserved, clear and specified, so that neither can transgress. It is best if this treaty between government and people be made with the knowledge of foreign powers, so they can be guarantors of this treaty.

order.why: Connect peaceful fellowship with a firm public covenant.
Retain the treatise’s distinction between both parties’ rights.
Read the constitutional proposal in its historical setting.
shortened: Every age has its requirements, and today's requirement is that governments be constitutional, as this brings comfort to the world of creation.

Therefore, constitutionalism is preferable, but utmost caution must be exercised so it does not become like other cases. There must be a treaty between the government and the people, with neighboring powers guaranteeing its observance. If violation occurs, there should be consequences. This is to prevent future difficulties.

order.why: Consider the reported account of ministerial accountability.
Keep the reported emphasis on election and public confidence.
Examine government’s role where labor disputes affect everyone.
Distinguish public retribution from private action in the source context.
shortened: In truth, undertaking that matter oneself was not permissible. However, the government has the right to carry out retribution through other means apart from the heir.

order.why: Hear the reported call for equal justice and opportunity.
Test rule by public works rather than private indulgence.
Hear the reported image of a neglected patient.
Consider spiritual accountability as an incentive to justice.
shortened: When a ruler knows that his judgments will be weighed in a balance by the Divine Judge, and that if he be not found wanting he will come into the Celestial Kingdom and that the light of the Heavenly Bounty will shine upon him, then will he surely act with justice and equity. Behold how important it is that Ministers of State should be enlightened by religion!

order.why: Extend the horizon of policy to humanity’s oneness.
shortened: Then divine policy shall govern the world, for the divine policy is the oneness of humanity. God is just and kind to all. He considers all as His servants. He excludes none, and His judgments are correct and true. No matter how complete human policy and foresight may appear, they are imperfect. If we do not seek the counsel of God or if we refuse to follow His dictates, it is presumptive evidence that we are knowing and wise, whereas God is ignorant; that we are sagacious and God is not.

order.why: Compare forms of government through their public purposes.
Retain the reported distinction between checks and selfish antagonism.
Read the report’s warning about self-interested constitutional officeholders.
shortened: The inhabitants of a nation must intelligently fulfill the requirements of the constitutional government and abide by all its conditions, otherwise it will bring upon them greater lawlessness and disintegration; for the reins will be taken out of the hands of an able, absolute Monarch and placed into the hands of a number of self-interested, useless parasites.

order.why: Preserve the reported answer about tyranny with its source status.
Place the hope for just laws in its Iranian context.
shortened: Should this momentous matter, which is among the most important of all affairs, be established and promoted, there is no doubt that Iran will soon become prosperous and flourishing, and its honored people will progress day by day in modern advancements and ascend to the highest degrees of success and prosperity.

order.why: Hear the reported call for consultation about laws.
Consider consultation as a source of stability.
shortened: Soon you will observe that these disturbing events will pass away and the government will become firmly established and steadfast in utmost stability. Consultation will become the cause of firmness and steadfastness, especially a government whose confirmation and strengthening has been decreed by the Supreme Pen.

order.why: Read praise of parliament as conditional on justice and progress.
Consider the mutual benefit described for crown and nation.
Connect trust with faithful administration and public comfort.
shortened: Rather, both the government and the people should develop such trust that they would wish for all affairs in the provinces to be entrusted to the pure and goodly hands of the friends of God, and through this means Iran and Iranians would make rapid progress and the means of comfort and ease would be provided for all peoples.

order.why: Retain the hope for general benefit from wise governance.
shortened: And it is hoped from the sympathies and favors of the Glorious Lord that general benefits and good fruits will result from their excellent conduct and wise governance.

order.why: Keep the contemporary assessment of Iran’s governing body.
Read the instruction to seek permission in its particular setting.
Preserve the refusal to enter political affairs.
Read the call to restrain clerical aggression historically.
Connect the treatise with noninterference by religious leaders.
Retain the letter’s polemical historical comparison without generalizing it.
Bring obedience and just treatment into the same appeal.
shortened: This conflict and strife and discord between the government and people is causing the ruin of Iran. I beseech God that the people obey the government and the government deal justly with the people.

order.why: Restate the importance of connection between people and government.
Recall the warning given before the war.
shortened: Before the war it was written, that is, in explicit terms in 'Abdu'l-Baha's own hand, that government and people must mix like honey and milk, otherwise Iran would be laid waste, and so forth.

order.why: Connect internal division with outside interference.
Read the repeated warning in the letter’s retrospective account.
shortened: Similarly, it was written time and again that until the government and people blend together like milk and honey, prosperity and success would be impossible and unattainable. The letters exist, and even in several detailed letters to Tehran it was explicitly written, including to the Shah's trusted confidant, that if the government and people do not blend together and unite, affairs would become entirely disordered and neighboring powers would intervene.

order.why: Make reconciliation and avoidance of bloodshed explicit.
Keep the parallel warning and withdrawal instruction.
Read the repeated call to reconciliation.
shortened: Especially 'Abdu'l-Baha, at the beginning of the revolution and conflict between government and people, wrote explicitly to Tehran repeatedly, and these are the exact words: "Government and people must mix together like honey and milk, otherwise success and prosperity are impossible.
Therefore the friends of God must strive with heart and soul to bring about reconciliation between government and people, and if they remain powerless, they must withdraw.

order.why: Preserve the reported version of that instruction.
shortened: However, from the beginning of the revolution, the emphatic statements of the Center of the Covenant to the people of Baha were repeatedly of this kind: that until the government and people mix like milk and honey, progress and prosperity are impossible and unattainable.
Therefore, O loved ones of God, strive so that complete harmony and unity may be achieved between the government and people, and if you remain powerless, withdraw completely.

order.why: Keep the reported warning against foreign encroachment.
shortened: We wrote and exhorted them, pointing out that the union of government and the people is like combining milk and honey; otherwise, the neighboring governments will encroach upon the country.

order.why: Hear the reported early call for cooperation.
Retain the explicit reference to the Constitutional Revolution.
shortened: At the outset of that revolution in Persia known as the Constitutional Revolution, I wrote again and again that until such time as that government and its people become commingled, even as milk and honey, their success and prosperity will remain entirely unattainable.

order.why: Return to the milk-and-sugar image.
shortened: We have written repeatedly that government and people must blend together like milk and sugar, otherwise progress and prosperity are impossible and unattainable.

order.why: Preserve the letter’s concise quotation of the principle.
shortened: Among these is this passage: "Until government and people blend together like honey and milk, prosperity and salvation are impossible.

order.why: Link cooperation with peace and purpose.
shortened: And it was written repeatedly that until the government and people mix with each other like milk and sugar, peace and purpose will not be achieved.

order.why: Hear goodwill toward both sides without joining contention.
Keep the report’s combination of constitutional concern and justice for a victim.
shortened: Because today a despotic government cannot be held any more, and until the Royalist and Nationalist can become blended as milk and sugar, tranquility and prosperity cannot be obtained, and further, you must proceed to punish those who martyred one of the Bahais, Seyid Yah Yah, in the city of Sirjan.

order.why: Read the prayer for restored connection historically.
Preserve the particular petition of gratitude to authorities.
shortened: Consequently, we in general, who are the well-wishers of the government and Persian nation, with utmost gratification are praising and commending the justice of His Royal Highness, the Prince, and are content and glad; and in order to manifest our thanks we present this petition; and whatever in the line of service is commanded us, we are ready to comply with the most extreme diligence. We ask earnestly from God that the Imperial Government become everlasting, His Imperial Majesty, the just Shah, remain and live long, and His Royal Highness, the Prince, become to every subject a divine gift and that he may become confirmed and helped in all affairs."

order.why: Turn personal counsel toward compassion for the people.
Keep the prayer concerning ruler and ruled.
Translate civic connection into sympathetic hearts.
Read reported cooperation as a response to justice.
Retain the alternate reported formulation without silently repairing its wording.
Close linked readings with advancement for government and nation.
Add the supplied call for equal treatment across rank.
Close with the supplied historical warning about divided public life.

questions: How do the passages connect a government’s strength with the welfare of its people?
What distinguishes mutual trust from obedience that has no reciprocal protection?
How do defined rights, consultation, and accountability give practical form to harmony?
What can be learned from the historically situated warnings about faction and intervention without treating every proposal as timeless?
Why might Confucius place public confidence above other necessities, and what questions does that comparison raise?
How can a person contribute to reconciliation while taking injustice and the common good seriously?

references.label: 1 · Confucius, Analects XII.7 · The people’s confidence
references.note: In James Legge’s translation, Confucius names food, military equipment, and the people’s confidence as requirements of government. Asked what could be surrendered, he places confidence last. Compare this striking priority with the compilation’s relationship of justice, cooperation, and prosperity. The Analects passage concerns the foundation of rule; it does not specify the constitutional safeguards and reciprocal agreements proposed in several of these letters.

subjects.displayTitle: The Crimson Ark: belonging, guidance, and steadfastness
subjects.introduction: No wind can shake it, no sea can drown it, no rock can shatter it: Bahá’u’lláh describes an Ark that crosses both land and sea, whose captain is the Will of God and whose passengers are the people of Bahá. To speak of a community as an ark is to say something about belonging that other images leave out. One does not build it or steer it; one recognises it, embarks, and holds on through the storm, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá makes the Covenant itself that vessel of salvation, with a Navigator who must be followed. Who, then, is aboard? Whoever has recognised God in this day, whoever has caught the fragrance of the verses, and those who stand firm even if no other assured soul remains on earth. Patience, forbearance and service turn a place on deck into a responsibility. First Peter reads Noah’s ark through baptism and the resurrection of Christ [1], a reminder that an ark has carried different meanings for different communities. The voyage continues into firmness in the Covenant, the high station of the true believer, and the wider workings of symbolism in sacred speech.
subjects.arc: Begin with the extraordinary vessel, seek its guidance, then explore the qualities and responsibilities of those who embark.

order.why: Open with the striking Ark that crosses land and sea.
shortened: This is not a ship that can be shaken by the winds, or drowned by the seas, or shattered by the rocks. By God! This is the Ark of God that traverseth both land and sea, whose captain is the Will of the All-Merciful, and whose passengers are the people of Baha in all creation. Exalted be God, its Maker and Creator, the All-Wise, the All-Informed.

order.why: Connect the vessel directly with the Covenant.
shortened: For the world of existence is like unto an ocean and the essence of the Covenant is the Ark of Salvation leading to the realm on high.

order.why: Introduce the responsibility to follow the Navigator.
Join embarking with steadfastness even when alone.
shortened: Stand thou firm in the Cause in such wise that, though all in the heavens and on the earth should war against thee, and there be upon the earth no assured one save thyself, thou wouldst arise of thine own self for the Cause. This is God's command unto thee; and His command encompasseth all worlds. Embark thou upon the Crimson Ark in My Most High, Most Exalted Name; then sail upon the sea of majesty, that thou mayest be numbered among the people of Baha in the Mother Book.

order.why: Hear the reported refusal to turn aside at danger.
shortened: If I were to hesitate or change direction at the sight of every danger, the Ark of the Cause of God would surely fail to reach its destination.

order.why: Read protection through the image of surviving tempest.
Let the vessel begin its voyage on the ocean of Names.
shortened: Thus doth the Most Exalted Pen proclaim: Rejoice, O people of faithfulness, for the Crimson Ark hath sailed upon the ocean of Names, and the people of Baha have embarked thereon by the leave of God, the Almighty, the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Connect its movement with the ocean of oneness.
Hear the invitation to enter in the divine Name.
Define companionship through recognition.
shortened: Today, whosoever hath attained unto the recognition of God is recorded in the Divine Book as one of the people of the Crimson Ark.

order.why: Connect recognition with hearing the verses.
shortened: They who have inhaled the fragrance of the verses when the Dawning-Place of clear proofs appeared, they are the companions of the Crimson Ark before God, the Lord of what was and what shall be.

order.why: Read the contrast between receptivity and obstructed perception.
Locate the transition from the Bayan to the people of Bahá.
Introduce the explicit reference to the Qayyúmu’l-Asmá’.
Read the parallel declaration of companions.
shortened: These are they who are the companions of the Crimson Ark, as recorded by the Most Exalted Pen in the Qayyumu'l-Asma'.

order.why: Hear praise grounded in the same textual reference.
shortened: Glory and praise be upon the people of the Crimson Ark, mention of which was revealed in the Qayyumu'l-Asma' before God, the One, the Chosen One.

order.why: Connect turning toward revelation with that reference.
shortened: And they who have turned towards it are among the people of the Crimson Ark, whom God hath mentioned in the Qayyumu'l-Asma.

order.why: Retain its appearance in a particular person’s recognition.
Links the Crimson Ark with fear of God and virtuous conduct.
Keep the further affirmation in the Supreme Pen’s language.
Turn the remembered Ark into a prayer for fitting action.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O King of Kings and Merciful to the servants, by Thy Name before which all names bow down in adoration, and by the light of Thy countenance before which all on earth and in heaven humble themselves, and by the Crimson Ark which Thou didst ordain especially for the people of Baha in the Qayyumu'l-Asma', to assist me in Thy remembrance and praise and enable me to do what befitteth Thy days.

order.why: Make service to others a purpose of supplication.
Identify patience and forbearance as qualities of companionship.
shortened: Today a spiritual messenger brought from the garden of inner meanings these words: "Whosoever is victorious through patience and forbearance in times of hardship and adversity, he is of the people of Baha and the companions of the Crimson Ark.

order.why: Connect hearing with arising to serve.
shortened: Others have succeeded in hearing the rustling of the Divine Lote Tree and the shrill voice of the Supreme Pen, and have arisen to serve the Cause in such wise that God Himself bears witness: these are the people of the Crimson Ark whose names have been inscribed by the Supreme Pen in the Crimson Book.

order.why: Read fidelity despite censure.
shortened: The glory from Us be upon the people of Baha who have held fast to the Crimson Ark and whom the censure of every denier and deceiver hath not kept from the Path.

order.why: Offer consolation amid what has befallen the community.
shortened: O people of Baha! Be not grieved by what hath befallen you in creation. By God! Ye are the companions of the Crimson Ark.

order.why: Keep the rejoicing over a particular arrival at prison.
Extend greeting and illumination to family and companions.
shortened: Convey My greetings to thy family and to those who have held fast to the Crimson Ark. Then illumine them with the lights that have shone forth and appeared from this manifest horizon.

order.why: Hear the prayer not to be deprived.
shortened: We beseech God not to deprive the people of Baha from the Crimson Ark.

order.why: Read personal longing to be a companion.
shortened: I beseech Him, exalted be He, to make me one of the companions of the Crimson Ark which hath adorned the sea of grandeur when He came Who illumined thereby the Most Exalted Horizon.

order.why: Seek what will profit through the divine bounty.
Connect guidance, utterance and holding fast.
shortened: We make mention of those who turned to God when the ocean of utterance appeared with manifest waves, and We guide them to the Ark which We have fashioned with the hands of Our power that dominates all who are in the heavens and on earth. Hold fast unto it, O people of Baha, and follow not every heedless and remote one.

order.why: Hear the call addressed to the Ark’s people.
shortened: O people of the Crimson Ark! Hearken unto the call of your Lord, the Most Glorious, from this Most Sublime Horizon: Verily, there is none other God but Me, the Single, the All-Informed.

order.why: Read their joy at the establishment of glory.
shortened: Through Him was opened the gate of mysteries, and the trees did speak, and the Herald called out from every direction: "O denizens of the highest Paradise and the most exalted Garden! The eyes of the people of the Crimson Ark have been gladdened by the establishment of the Glory upon the throne of faithfulness.

order.why: Retain the blessing upon those settled aboard.
Connect boarding with certitude.
Keep the parallel affirmation in the divine Name.
shortened: Verily the glory be upon the people of Baha who are established upon the Crimson Ark through the name of God, the Possessor of Names.

order.why: Read joy together with detachment.
shortened: By God! They are in a state of joy and delight, and they are servants who have embarked upon the Crimson Ark in My Most Great Name and have detached themselves from the world.

order.why: Connect holding fast with nearness.
shortened: Verily the glory be upon the people of Baha who have held fast unto the Crimson Ark and drawn nigh unto God, the One, the All-Informed.

order.why: Join the Ark with the paradise of knowledge.
shortened: He is of the people of the paradise of My knowledge and the companions of My Ark, which the All-Merciful hath mentioned in His perspicuous Book.

order.why: Place the Ship of Salvation beside the Tree of Life.
shortened: However high the waves of tests may rise, they shall not reach the passengers of the Ark of the Covenant. This is the Ship of Salvation, this is the Tree of Life.

order.why: Preserve the direct question addressed to the sea.
Keep companionship and inscription together.
Read the Book of Names as another image of recognition.
Retain the affirmation in the perspicuous Book.
shortened: These are they who are truly of the people of Baha and the companions of the Crimson Ark which God hath mentioned in His perspicuous Book.

order.why: Preserve the particular person’s remembrance.
Keep the concise statement of belonging.
shortened: Happy is he who witnessed the great words and happy is he who speaks what God commands him to speak. Verily, he is among the people of the Crimson Ark in a clear Book.

order.why: Retain the Tablet’s testimony concerning a companion.
shortened: Such a one is numbered among the companions of the Crimson Ark, as attested by the Lord of Names and Creator of the heavens in this blessed, mighty and wondrous Tablet.

order.why: Preserve the further affirmation of companionship.
Keep the collective recognition.
shortened: Blessed are they who have attained unto the cord of true oneness and held fast thereunto. These are the people of Baha and the companions of the Crimson Ark.

order.why: Read inscription within all-encompassing knowledge.
Connect the Ark with the Concourse on High.
shortened: Whoso attains unto it is of the Concourse on High and the companions of My Crimson Ark, by which the Books have been adorned.

order.why: Place the wine of utterance beside the Crimson Tablet.
Retain the contrast between attainment and deprivation.
Acknowledge language whose comprehension is reserved to God.
shortened: To this bears witness the Lord of Eternity in this station which has been named by all names in the Crimson Tablet which none has comprehended save the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Read the eschatological glad-tidings in their own setting.
shortened: In this day the Sun of Truth, from the horizon of the prison of 'Akka, speaketh this most sublime Word: I say in truth, the blessed word "but He is the Apostle of God and the Seal of the Prophets" found its consummation in "the Day when mankind shall stand before the Lord of the worlds." This is the Most Great Glad-Tidings for the Concourse on High and the companions of the Crimson Ark and for whosoever is in the heavens and the earth.

order.why: Preserve the trumpet image and its exceptions.
Read attainment and remoteness as contrasting spiritual positions.
shortened: He who hath attained on this Day is, before God, his Lord, the Most Exalted, the Most Glorious, among the companions of the Crimson Ark, and he who hath been prevented is among the most remote of creatures in a hidden Tablet.

order.why: Read the sharp contrast of rescue and drowning symbolically.
Carry the voyage toward return to God.
shortened: Soon shall every soul return to its resting-place, and the people of Baha shall be with their Lord, riding upon the Crimson Ark.

order.why: Close linked readings with a greeting to the companions.
shortened: Glory be upon the people of Baha and the companions of the Crimson Ark.

order.why: Echo the blessing from God.
End with the supplied Báb passage underlying the recurring imagery.

How do recognition, guidance, and steadfastness shape the meaning of embarking?
What do the passages on patience and service add to the descriptions of a high spiritual station?
How might the connected subject of the Covenant deepen a reading of the Navigator?
How does First Peter transform the ark image, and where does its Christian interpretation differ from these passages?
