references.label: 1 · 1 Peter 3:18–22 · Noah’s ark and baptism
references.note: First Peter recalls the few who were saved through water in Noah’s ark and connects that event with baptism, conscience before God, and Christ’s resurrection. Compare the movement from a vessel to spiritual meaning with the Crimson Ark’s associations of recognition, guidance, and the Covenant. The Christian passage has a specific account of salvation through Christ; it should not be treated as assigning the same meaning to every ark image.

subjects.displayTitle: The call to unity: making reconciliation a form of service
subjects.introduction: Among the greatest services, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, is the unification of hearts. That ranking changes the character of unity: it is not a mood to be enjoyed but labour to be undertaken, in the next conversation and the grievance left unresolved. Bahá’u’lláh warns the peoples of the earth not to make religion a cause of enmity, observes that all that flourishes springs from fellowship while ruin stems from hatred, and admits that the fragrance of this station has still not been detected among his own friends. A community cannot heal a sick world while quarrelling within itself; no one should interfere with or object to another; where affection fails, the result is separation and regret. The Qur’an’s appeal to hold together to God’s rope, remembering enemies made brothers by divine grace, offers a kindred image of reconciliation [1]. The call widens to religious rivalry, racial and national prejudice, and the bond between governments and peoples. It leads on into love and fellowship among the friends, the role of the Covenant in preserving unity, and the oneness of humanity.
subjects.arc: Begin with reconciliation as service, examine the community’s own life, and widen the call toward the removal of prejudice and conflict.

order.why: Read unity as a power against tyranny.
Open by naming the unification of hearts as great service.
shortened: All must occupy themselves with unifying hearts and be detached and free from all else but God. A hundred thousand blessings upon the soul that hath today arisen to serve the Cause, for service hath degrees and ranks. Among the greatest services is the unification of hearts. The successful and sincere ones must turn to this mighty matter, that the effulgences of the Sun of unity may illumine their hearts. We have counseled all, both before and after, to unity.

order.why: Confront the misuse of religion as a source of enmity.
Set flourishing and ruin beside love and hatred.
Connect public healing with harmony within the community.
shortened: O friends, know that the believers of God must be the cause of union and love among all mankind, and until they attain to perfect harmony and agreement they will not become the remedy for the healing of this sick world.

order.why: Make the local need for union explicit.
shortened: O Ye sons and daughters of the kingdom! The most pressing need today is harmony and union among the friends of God. Therein endeavour, not until this unity in particular is realised can universal harmony be established.

order.why: Challenge the contradiction of arguing over a call to peace.
Hear the admission that the ideal remains unrealized.
shortened: The gaze of favor has been and God willing shall continue to be directed towards him. We have commanded and continue to command all the friends to unity and harmony, yet still the fragrance of this most exalted station has not been detected.

order.why: Turn recognition of discord toward active repair.
shortened: Despite this, the friends are quarreling and occupied with disputes among themselves.
You must strive with utmost effort to completely remove this discord and establish love and affection.

order.why: Ask for effort directed toward agreement.
Carry affection into every encounter.
shortened: The believers in the West must constantly strive for harmony and concord and be a source of affection and love to everyone they encounter.

order.why: Join harmony with equity and beneficence.
Connect fellowship with wisdom in conduct and speech.
shortened: Today they must conduct themselves with perfect unity, fellowship and wisdom, and in all circumstances speak in remembrance of the Beloved of all creation.

order.why: Link education and shared service with avoiding discord.
shortened: United, in harmony, and detached unto God, we must strive to diffuse the divine fragrances and educate souls, and we must avoid whatever causes the least discord.

order.why: Retain the particular instruction against interference and objection.
shortened: The most important matter today is unity and harmony. No one should interfere with or object to another.

order.why: Read the strong warning against openings to division.
shortened: You must absolutely avoid anything that could cause even an atom of discord. Never allow anyone to create an opening even as small as a hair's breadth that could lead to division and dispersion.

order.why: Keep the responsibility to remove differences among friends.
shortened: According to His command: those souls who are today associated with the Truth and adorned with the lights of recognition must strive to remove differences, for no harm has been or will be greater than discord between the friends.

order.why: Place sincerity beside setting right mutual differences.
Connect discord with weakness and unity with strength.
shortened: The cause of weakness among the people of unity hath been discord. Now all must hold fast to the cord of unity and concord, that perchance the hidden glory may be made manifest and weakness be transformed into strength.

order.why: Associates unity with prosperity and warns against discord.
Read the cost of failing to act together.
shortened: Until the friends become as one being and move in complete unity, they will find no rest or tranquility, but rather will become scattered and dispossessed.

order.why: Keep the warning of separation without affection.
shortened: In any case, you can remove this cloudiness and establish love and affection.
And if affection is not established, the inevitable result will be separation, dispersion, regret and remorse.

order.why: Widen the warning across ages.
Preserve the situated polemical plea for protection from discord.
Read trials in relation to unity and the text’s stated bounds.
Hear the reported question about the fruit of sacrifice.
shortened: Is it possible to conceive that all the troubles, all the trials of Baha'u'llah and the martyrs have been without result? Surely you will not have it so! If you would all act entirely in accordance with the Teachings of Baha'u'llah no discord would ever appear. Then all disagreements will vanish, and be certain that the pavilion of Unity will be hoisted in the world of man.

order.why: Let the repeated invitations to love and peace gather force.
shortened: For the Greatest Name and the Ancient Beauty--may my soul be a sacrifice to His beloved--endured all difficulty and ordeals for the purpose of uniting the hearts of the beloved of God; that they might be exhilarated through the wine of unity and proclaim with one voice:
"Hasten to love, to love, O people of the world!
Hasten to harmony, to harmony, O creatures of the universe!
Hasten to peace, to peace, O mankind!
Hasten to safety, to safety, O concourse of the Divine!
Hasten to concord, to concord, O hosts of the Merciful!

order.why: Receive the accompanying prayer for united hearts.
Make a particular gathering a night of unity.
shortened: God willing, we hope that you will make this blessed night the night of unity, and all become united with one another, adorned with the ornament of praiseworthy virtues and excellent character.

order.why: Explore waves, flowers and trees as images of shared life.
shortened: In order to tender thanks for this gift, you must become engaged in creating harmony and union to such an extent that all of you may become as one soul and one spirit; that you may become as waves of one sea, breezes of one rose-garden, flowers of one meadow and trees of one orchard.

order.why: Retain the address to a particular assembly in its context.
Connect the call to unity with the Covenant.
shortened: O herald of the Covenant! Blessed art thou for having grasped the cord stretched forth from the Most Glorious Kingdom, and raised the banner of steadfastness upon the hills in the realms of God, and lifted high the word of unity, and brought low the standard of discord, and called out among the peoples of the horizons: "Hasten to the Covenant!

order.why: Link community fellowship with the foundation of religion.
Imagine local example drawing hostile peoples together.
shortened: The divine friends must manifest such unity under the shade of the Word of Oneness that the fragrances of that unity and oneness will gather together the different, opposing, conflicting and hostile nations of the world at the banks of the divine sea of oneness.

order.why: Name the prejudices that must be removed.
shortened: Then the Gardener of divine bounty will attend to pruning the flowers of realities and significances in the flowerbeds of the gardens of that country, and remove the thorns and weeds of religious and racial, national and personal, prejudices. And then the roses of unity of the human species, and of love and union will bloom.

order.why: Hear the reported answer about removing causes of division.
shortened: Abdul Baha's answer was: When you remove the causes thereof. These causes are racial, patriotic and religious bias or prejudice. This bias will be removed and when it is removed, people will live in friendliness, kindness and love which will bring forth unity.

order.why: Consider the reported role of misunderstanding.
Give reverence for others’ religious leaders a practical place.
Read the reported example of fellowship among denominations.
shortened: He caused fellowship and agreement to exist between the representatives of varying denominations so that love became manifest among the contending religions. He created a condition of harmony among hostile sects and upheld the banner of the oneness of the world of humanity.

order.why: Preserve the report’s appeal to Christ’s teaching.
shortened: Had the principles of unity, taught by the Christ, remained in the hearts, men would have refrained from war. Universalism must be retaught.

order.why: Consider gatherings that build friendship across races.
Hear the reported encouragement to embody brotherhood.
shortened: Thus I hope that you will cling to this love, become the cause of the appearance of this love, become the dawning-place of the shining forth of this brotherhood, become the means of spreading these fragrances, so that the bounties of Baha'u'llah may become manifest in the human world and divine favors may encompass all.

order.why: Keep the concise reported warning against separation.
Extend responsibility to leaders of humanity.
shortened: The leaders of mankind must at all time work for the spread of the principles of Unity. Unity is the light that illumineth every path. Our origin has been one and our end must be also one.

order.why: Include harmony between government and people.
shortened: In any case, despite this, we seek peace and harmony and consistently call for unity and concord. We have written repeatedly that government and people must blend together like milk and sugar, otherwise progress and prosperity are impossible and unattainable.

order.why: Widen service to every direction of the earth.
Hear the prisoner’s hope that fellowship will remove wider discord.
Spread the image of fellowship and universal love.
Gather peoples and places in a prayer for harmony.
shortened: O Lord! Thy counsels have spread far and wide to the East and West of the earth. Thou hast called all to love and harmony, to abandon discord throughout the world, that the East and West of the earth might embrace, that the peoples of the earth, both nomad and settled, might clasp hands, their dispersed elements be gathered, their disheveled state be put in order, their darkness be dispelled and their light shine forth.

order.why: Read humanity’s oneness as the stated goal.
shortened: Beyond this it is obvious and observable, in the written Divine and indisputable tablets that the primary Divine Principal and goal, The Holy Will of God, is none other than the unity of all the peoples of the world, that the Oneness of the entire human race, composed of all the diverse, antagonistic and distinct ethnic groups prevails to the extent that God's Word "Unity" is embodied and characterized on all levels, so that this earthy kingdom mirrors the Heavenly Kingdom.

order.why: Consider revelation’s light gathering hostile peoples.
Carry unity to the scale of the whole earth.
shortened: O thou that hast remembered Me! The most grievous veil hath shut out the peoples of the earth from His glory, and hindered them from hearkening to His call. God grant that the light of unity may envelop the whole earth, and that the seal “the Kingdom is God’s” may be stamped upon the brow of all its peoples.

order.why: Join removal of discord with illumination of hearts and minds.
Read reform of souls and union of nations together.
shortened: God is aware and mankind doth witness that this Wronged One hath, from the earliest days until now, striven mightily to reform souls and unite hearts, that the horizons of the world might be illumined with the light of concord among nations, and that all might turn with spirit and joy toward the Supreme Horizon and occupy themselves with that which profiteth their souls.

order.why: Keep the direct call for sustained effort.
shortened: That soul and other loved ones must hold fast to the improvement of the world and the removal of differences between peoples, and must exert mighty efforts.

order.why: Read the repeated counsel as an expression of care.
Situate the call within the text’s long horizon.
shortened: From time immemorial hath the True One summoned the people unto unity and concord.

order.why: Hear unity as the recurring message of the words.
Turn the reading into a prayer for shared illumination.
Close the linked argument with the dignity of time spent reconciling.
shortened: Beseech thou God that He may gather all beneath the shadow of one Word.
Whosoever in this day spendeth his time in promoting concord and unity among souls is recorded in God's Book as one of the bearers of His Throne.

order.why: Let the short injunction remain as a final refrain.
shortened: O friends! Hold fast unto unity and harmony.

order.why: End with the supplied call to remove estrangement through service.
shortened: In most of the Tablets We have commanded all the friends to unity and harmony, for from a collective body another effect becomes manifest and a special influence becomes evident.
All must gird up the loins of service and remove estrangements and differences from among themselves.

questions: What changes when uniting hearts is understood as a form of service requiring effort?
How can a community recognize contradictions between its message of unity and its own habits?
Which passages identify causes of discord, and how might those causes be addressed?
How do equity, sincerity, and the Covenant shape the meaning of agreement in these readings?
What does the Qur’anic memory of enemies becoming brothers contribute to the understanding of reconciliation?
What might a sustained practice of unity look like in a relationship or gathering you know?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 3:103 · Holding together and remembering reconciliation
references.note: This verse calls believers to hold together to God’s rope and recalls divine grace joining former enemies as brothers. Compare its combination of shared allegiance, gratitude, and repaired relationships with the compilation’s call to unite hearts. The Qur’anic address has its own communal and theological setting; the comparison also invites attention to how the Bahá’í passages extend their appeal toward all peoples and religions.

subjects.displayTitle: Courtesy: the dignity of everyday encounters
subjects.introduction: Do not enter a friend’s house except at his pleasure. Courtesy begins with that small act of restraint and grows, in Bahá’u’lláh’s words, into a raiment that fits all people, young or old, and the prince of virtues; without it a person is naked though dressed in all the silk of the earth. It is never a surface alone. Truthfulness, trustworthiness, justice and forbearance are its constant companions, so that respect for another’s dignity is also honesty toward them. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá shows the quality in motion: welcoming a workman with a smile, telling the friends to treat prominent strangers with perfect dignity, counselling gentleness and moderation, refusing to be rude to any human being. A Bedouin host who spreads his only carpet for a guest, a letter of thanks, a difficult debt and a delicate relationship show how differently the same respect can be expressed. Confucius’s question about ritual propriety in a person lacking humane virtue tests outward form by inner character from another tradition [1]. The way continues into hospitality, into wisdom as the companion of speech, and into the refinement that makes outward life beautiful.
subjects.arc: Begin with respect for another person’s wishes, connect manners to character, and explore courtesy in speech, hospitality, and difficult relationships.

order.why: Present courtesy as a garment for every age.
Open with consent and refusal to take advantage.
Reinforce permission and humility across differences of wealth.
shortened: Say: Beware lest ye enter anyone's house except with his permission, and beware lest ye pride yourselves over any of My servants by reason of what ye have been given of the ornaments of the earth.

order.why: Recounts the courtesy and kindness shown by Baha’u’llah in His dealings in Iraq.
Hear its elevated place among virtues.
Connect outward conduct with truthfulness and fidelity.
shortened: Adorn your heads with the garlands of trustworthiness and fidelity, your hearts with the attire of the fear of God, your tongues with absolute truthfulness, your bodies with the vesture of courtesy. These are in truth seemly adornings unto the temple of man, if ye be of them that reflect.

order.why: Bring justice and forbearance into the same moral fabric.
shortened: Say: Let truthfulness and courtesy be your adorning. Suffer not yourselves to be deprived of the robe of forbearance and justice, that the sweet savors of holiness may be wafted from your hearts upon all created things.

order.why: Unite speech, generosity, dignity and love.
Keep wisdom and trustworthiness beside courtesy.
shortened: O people of Baha! Adorn your temples with the ornament of trustworthiness and courtesy, and your heads with the crown of truthfulness and wisdom.

order.why: Connect conduct with assistance to the Cause.
shortened: O, `Ali, assist your Lord by your conduct and character. This is worthy of those who cling to this Strong Cord. Adorn your bodies with the robe of courtesy, and your hearts with mention of Me, the Almighty, the Incomparable.

order.why: Read courtesy as a human characteristic and divine bounty.
Contrast propriety with merely luxurious clothing.
Hear the restraint against discourteous speech.
shortened: This Youth hath ever been disinclined to breathe a word contrary to courtesy, for courtesy is Our raiment, wherewith We have adorned the temples of Our well-favoured servants.

order.why: Make cheerful kindness a fundamental practice.
Place joy and mercy at the center of encounter.
shortened: As much as you can, be a source of joy and delight and a manifestation of the mercy of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Hear the reported consolation of a cheerful face.
See welcome offered to a workman.
shortened: A workman who had left his bag of tools in the hall was welcomed with smiling kindness by 'Abdu'l-Baha. With a look of sadness the man said: "I don't know much about religious things, as I have no time for anything but my work."
"That is well. Very well.

order.why: Make kindness toward a visitor an explicit expectation.
Extend good conduct across peoples and religions.
Read praise of hospitality to friend and stranger.
Consider service and love toward pilgrims.
shortened: In utmost calm and composure busy yourself with service to the House, and treat the pilgrims with the utmost love and kindness so that they become grateful and happy with you.

order.why: Retain the particular welcome to American visitors.
Connect welcome with practical letters of recommendation.
Preserve the request for consideration along a journey.
Keep the courteous invitation to a gathering.
Read the reported hospitality story as a historically situated example.
Extend kindness across rank and familiarity.
shortened: I beseech God that day by day they may increase in this firmness and steadfastness and walk this path in such wise that they may attract both the master and servant, and deal with both friend and stranger with the utmost kindness, truthfulness and friendship.

order.why: Keep the particular greeting to Tolstoy.
shortened: Always extend to Count Tolstoy loving and heartfelt greetings and treat him with the utmost courtesy, as we are indeed commanded to behave in this way.

order.why: Distinguish kind counsel from harsh pressure.
shortened: It behooves ones like yourself to deal with all souls with kindness and consideration.
Regarding deeds, give counsel with kindness as 'Abdu'l-Baha has written, not with force, intensity and harshness, for harshness and intensity never yield fruit but rather have the opposite effect.

order.why: Consider how gentleness affects the reception of counsel.
shortened: O brother, be honey and sugar sweet, and sweeten dispositions to the extent possible. Forbearance is necessary, lest any dust settle on a heart or any soul be hurt. Then all effort would be fruitless. If counsel is given with perfect gentleness and kindness and utmost humility and goodwill, it will have a mighty effect.

order.why: Hear the reported connection between kindness and listening.
Read the image of sweet speech affecting stone.
shortened: Good conduct and sweet speech can influence even the hardest stone, and it is certain that thou hast carried out and will continue to carry out this matter.

order.why: Pause with the concise counsel to speak gently.
Consider praise, silence and the avoidance of unkind words.
Keep the reported counsel about speech and writing.
Consider timing when bearing difficult news.
shortened: On the other hand, if ye have a bad message or news for a certain person, show ye no haste in conveying it, and trouble not the heart of the concerned individual.

order.why: Explore courtesy through concise and useful correspondence.
shortened: O faithful servant of the Beauty of Abha!

The perfumed letter from that longtime friend was in the utmost eloquence, fluency and brevity. A letter should be thus - few in words but rich in meaning, eloquent in meaning, fluent in expression, concise and beneficial.

order.why: Retain gratitude for a received letter.
shortened: Some time ago your missive arrived and bestowed its portion upon the eye, heart, ear and breast, each according to its capacity. God bless your honor!

order.why: Keep the courteous acknowledgment of writing.
Connect speaking in an assembly with others’ permission.
shortened: Should anyone desire to speak, he must do it with the utmost courtesy and with perfect eloquence and fluency by the consent and permission of the people of the assembly.

order.why: Read attention to readiness, wisdom and deference.
shortened: Whenever they see that a capability is created, they may speak with wisdom and deference and utter the words with dignity and kindness.

order.why: Preserve the instruction to treat others with dignity in its setting.
shortened: As this place is a summer resort and many prominent people are present, therefore, unless they should themselves ask, the friends should not teach openly. They must deal with them with perfect dignity and honor.

order.why: Hear the reported breadth of dignified social conduct.
shortened: One's sitting and rising, speech and conversation, social intercourse and communication should be based upon a firm foundation and be conducive to the glory of the world of humanity.

order.why: Give punctuality a place among everyday considerations.
Retain the simple counsel for composure.
shortened: Walk thou in utmost dignity and composure.

order.why: Keep the reported universal rejection of rudeness.
shortened: We must adorn our temples with extreme politeness. We must not be rude to any human being.

order.why: Explore courtesy within a delicate relationship and risk of misunderstanding.
Preserve the particular instruction concerning Shaykh’ur-Ra’is.
shortened: Regarding Shaykh'ur-Ra'is, the friends must remain quiet and silent and, in accordance with the divine texts, act with the utmost spiritual courtesy.

order.why: Read moderation and gentleness beside restraint.
shortened: If they respond, God will illumine their faces, and if they refuse, leave them to themselves and never move your tongue to mention them. Every soul knows its own salvation, and no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. Leave them, leave them, and practice moderation and gentleness.

order.why: Keep tolerance and benevolence together.
shortened: But the loved ones must adopt a manner and conduct that attracts hearts, not causes souls to flee. They must be gentle and forbearing, patient and tolerant, and deal with all souls - whether righteous or wicked - with kindness and courtesy. They must show tolerance and be benevolent.

order.why: Consider another person’s satisfaction as a test of character.
shortened: In any case, act in such a way that he too becomes satisfied with you. Then the expansiveness of your character will become evident and clear.

order.why: Bring good conduct into a concrete debt disagreement.
Keep the particular diplomatic instruction.
shortened: Meet with His Excellency the Ambassador with utmost courtesy so that they may arise to fulfill what they have mentioned and return may be possible with perfect love.

order.why: Read formal thanks and apology in an official letter.
shortened: Most great minister, most mighty and noble ambassador, may your prosperity endure, I wish to mention that a petition was written and that, at the time it was sent, your excellency's second letter brought joy to the hearts of these withered souls.
We hope that God may increase your excellency's life, prosperity, and glory at all times. I am most ashamed to have put your excellency to such trouble.

order.why: Consider reassurance about a gift that caused embarrassment.
Retain the counsel about association with prominent people.
shortened: And if you desire to associate with the great and mighty ones, adorn yourself with knowledge and wisdom and with the refinements they possess.

order.why: Read the instruction about speech and learning in context.
shortened: As for the rest, you must strongly urge his honor Mirza Muhammad Hadi - may God illumine his countenance - to remain preserved from the attributes and tongue of those people, meaning his speech should remain preserved from the accent [of Beg] and others, and in writing and knowledge they should certainly strive.

order.why: Turn toward the formation of courtesy in childhood.
shortened: The children must be carefully trained to be most courteous and well-behaved. They must be constantly encouraged and made eager to gain all the summits of human accomplishment, so that from their earliest years they will be taught to have high aims, to conduct themselves well, to be chaste, pure, and undefiled, and will learn to be of powerful resolve and firm of purpose in all things.

order.why: Connect refinement with ongoing moral aspiration.
shortened: The friends of God must, in every case, be the manifestation of perfection and be at the height of training and refinement.

order.why: Preserve the historical criticism of education without adopting its national generalization.
shortened: The people of Iran had no educator and reached maturity without training. Therefore their badge and garment have been and continue to be ignorance and discourtesy. Say: O people! The first ornament for the temple of man is courtesy. Hold fast unto it and be not of the heedless ones.

order.why: Keep the reported challenge about religious difference with its distinct status.
shortened: The Master: "O my daughter, you say that the unity of religion is not to be demonstrated and demanded as a necessity, on the contrary, you Occidentals say that people are so fundamentally different as to race, origin, heredity, cultural level, life-style, era, domicile, sex, that in this is already to be found the historic, scientific reason for the multiplicity of religious needs. O my daughter, these are pretexts! What is religion?

order.why: Close with the supplied distinction between respect and self-aggrandizement.

questions: Which small acts in these passages make another person’s dignity tangible?
How do truthfulness, justice, and trustworthiness change the meaning of courtesy?
What distinguishes gentle counsel from flattery or avoidance of a difficult truth?
How might courtesy take different forms when welcoming a stranger, resolving a debt, or speaking in a gathering?
How does Confucius’s question about humane virtue and ritual illuminate the relationship between inner character and outward form?
What can be learned from the particular letters while remaining attentive to their cultural and historical settings?

references.label: 1 · Confucius, Analects III.3 · Humanity and ritual propriety
references.note: In James Legge’s translation, Confucius questions the place of rites and music in someone lacking the virtues proper to humanity. Compare that test of outward practice by inner character with courtesy joined to justice and kindness here. Ritual propriety has a particular role in Confucian cultivation; it is not simply interchangeable with every use of courtesy or adab in the compilation.

subjects.displayTitle: Fire, light, and water: reading the transformations of a symbol
subjects.introduction: A fire can warm, illumine, consume, or turn out to be the very water that gives life. Bahá’u’lláh prays that his prayer may become a flame burning away the veils between him and his Beloved, and then tells us that this fire is inwardly light and inwardly water, the source from which all living things drink. The same element has a dark face: the fire that keeps a soul back from God is kindled by its own deeds, and no fire is fiercer than remoteness from Him. Learning to tell these fires apart, and to watch one image pass into another, is the whole art of reading here. Moses turning aside toward a bush that burns without being consumed, then taking off his shoes on holy ground, is the oldest model of such attention, and the Mount and the Fire of Sinai return again and again in the Bahá’í prayers [1]. From there the way leads naturally to the living waters that renew the heart, to love itself understood as a fire that no utterance can quench, and to the old insight that things are known by their opposites, so that cooling mercy and igniting love, tears and burning, are finally one gift.
subjects.arc: Begin with prayer’s transforming images, distinguish life-giving fire from remoteness, and follow illumination into recognition and conduct.

order.why: Open with prayer as fire, light and living water.
shortened: Then let him say:

O Thou Who art the Lord of all names and the Maker of the heavens! I beseech Thee by them Who are the Day-Springs of Thine invisible Essence, the Most Exalted, the All-Glorious, to make of my prayer a fire that will burn away the veils which have shut me out from Thy beauty, and a light that will lead me unto the ocean of Thy Presence.
Let him then stand and say:
Make my prayer, O my Lord, a fountain of living waters whereby I may live as long as Thy sovereignty endureth, and may make mention of Thee in every world of Thy worlds.

order.why: Introduce the paradox of fire that is inwardly light and water.
shortened: This fire is in truth water appearing in the form of fire - outwardly fire, inwardly light. Through this water all things have had and will have life, for "from water doth all life come."

order.why: Make the stated identity of fire and light explicit.
shortened: I pray to God that thou mayest at all times be enkindled with the fire of the love of the All-Merciful. This fire is in truth light, and light is identical with fire.

order.why: Distinguish guiding light from the fire attributed to one’s deeds.
shortened: My God, my God! Thy light calls me unto Thee, and Thy fire keeps me back from Thee. I testify that the light hath appeared and shone forth from Thy face, while the fire is from mine own deeds, though it is attributed to Thee for Thou didst create and manifest it.

order.why: Define the most intense fire as remoteness from God.
Read the different effects of turning toward or away.
shortened: Through the appearance of this word two universal effects became manifest in creation: fire and light. For whosoever turned toward it was accounted before God among the companions of the right hand who have attained the lights of His countenance, and whosoever turned away was mentioned as one of the people of fire.

order.why: Contrast a cooling drop of mercy with love’s igniting spark.
Hear the flame of love that utterance cannot extinguish.
shortened: Verily, I say, so fierce is the blaze of the Bush of love, burning in the Sinai of the heart, that the streaming waters of holy utterance can never quench its flame.

order.why: Read fire and water joined in a fountain of life.
Explains water and fire as symbols of knowledge and love.
Continue the conjunction in the Tablet of the Hair.
Consider the balance between tears and burning desire.
shortened: Thou hast Thyself, O my God, protected them, by Thy sovereign might, from both extremities. But for the burning of their souls and the sighing of their hearts, they would be drowned in the midst of their tears, and but for the flood of their tears they would be burnt up by the fire of their hearts and the heat of their souls. Methinks, they are like the angels which Thou hast created of snow and of fire.

order.why: Keep the petitioner’s uncertainty about the elements within.
shortened: I know not what the water is with which Thou didst create me, or what the fire Thou didst kindle within me.

order.why: Join preservation through water with remembrance as fire.
shortened: The waters of Thy love have preserved me in the kingdom of Thy creation, and the fire of my remembrance of Thee hath set me ablaze before all that are in heaven and on earth.

order.why: Read flowing mercy and burning kindness together.
Let the revealing Pen give both water and fire.
shortened: For he would, at one time, discover that from this Pen there floweth out unto all created things the water that is life indeed, and that the Pen itself hath been named by Thee the trumpet whereby the dead speed out of their sepulchers. At another time he would find that there proceedeth from this Pen such fire as Thine own Revelation can kindle, and as He Who conversed with Thee (Moses) on Sinai hath perceived.

order.why: Explore the successive manifestations of life-giving water and flame.
shortened: At one time He appeareth as the water which is Life indeed, sent down out of the heaven of Thy grace, and poured forth from the clouds of thy mercy, that Thy creatures may be endued with new life, and live as long as Thine own Kingdom endureth.

At another time He revealeth Himself as the Fire which Thou didst kindle in the tree of Thy unity, whose heat melted the hearts of Thine ardent lovers when He Who is the Day-Star of the world shone forth above the horizon of 'Iraq.

order.why: Connect life-giving fire with the Mount.
Read the allusion to Moses and removed attachments.
Keep the recognition of light from Sinai.
shortened: O servants of the Blessed Beauty! On the Day of Manifestation you acquired illumination from the lights of Mount Sinai and witnessed a gleam of radiance.

order.why: Preserve the letter’s testimony concerning the Fire.
shortened: O Bahram! Know this with absolute certainty. Firstly, He came with the Fire from the presence of the Friend and enkindled the extinguished element, and secondly, He gave His testimony concerning the Fire.

order.why: Hear the invitation from lamp and Tree.
Keep the brief announcement voiced by the Fire.
Distinguish a visible sign from the world-illumining reality.
Contrast a small human fire with the divine flame’s reach.
shortened: The fire lit by mortal hand imparteth light and warmth to but a little space, whereas that sacred flame which the Hand of God hath kindled, though burning in the east, will set aflame the west and give warmth to both the north and the south; nay, it shall rise from this world to glow with the hottest flame in the realms on high, flooding with light the Kingdom of eternal glory.

order.why: Read fire itself seeking illumination from the divine Countenance.
shortened: It is calling aloud at all times upon the branch of Fire within the hallowed and luminous garden of Paradise, that perchance the inmates of the realm of creation may detach themselves from the world of dust and ascend unto the retreats of nearness -- the Spot where the Fire seeketh illumination from the light of the Countenance of God, the Glorious, the Powerful.

order.why: Keep the Tablet of the Hair’s image of consumed hearts.
shortened: Glorified be God for this fiery thread and this divine cord! At times I behold it as fire, for by it are consumed the hearts of the sincere. At times I behold it as breezes, for by it are stirred the hearts of the believers. And at times there issueth from it a sound like unto melodies that draw unto them the hearts of the lovers.

order.why: Turn the Fire into a prayer for removal of veils.
shortened: Great is the blessedness of him that hath drawn nigh unto it, and heard its roaring.

I beseech Thee, O my Lord, by this Fire which blazeth and rageth in the world of creation, to rend asunder the veils that have hindered me from appearing before the throne of Thy majesty, and from standing at the door of Thy gate.

order.why: Join the consumption of veils with cleansing souls.
Trace the effects of guidance through the whole person.
shortened: O thou who art illumined by the light of divine guidance!

When the candle of guidance is kindled within the glass of the heart, it dispels the darkness of error that stems from worldly limitations. The lights of sanctification and the rays of unity shine upon all parts and members, senses and faculties.

order.why: Distinguish inference, vision and experienced certainty.
shortened: The similitude and example of this is this: that with reflection and rational proof, certainty about the existence of fire can be achieved, but when one seeth fire itself, that is then the station of the Eye of Certitude. When a human being gets ignited with that same fire or when one senses fully the heat of that fire, that is the station of the Reality of Certitude.

order.why: Consider what warmth and guidance answer in human limitation.
shortened: O yearning ones! If you are not enkindled by this divine fire that has been ignited, by what means will you dispel the cold of contingent being and the frigid conditions of human limitations? And if you are not illumined by this divine lamp that glows in the glass of the All-Merciful, by what light shall you be guided?

order.why: Move from heedlessness toward awakened perception.
shortened: You have awakened from the sleep of heedlessness and opened your eyes to witness the lights. You have been attracted to the Truth and been set ablaze by the fire kindled in the blessed Tree of the Lord. You have been delivered from darkness and reached the Dawning-place of lights.

order.why: Read an enduring enkindlement beyond doubt.
Place steadfastness beside the test of the Fire.
Explore moth, phoenix and ocean as devotional images.
shortened: The moth which is animated by love will burn its wings as it flitteth round the lamp of God, and the phoenix of tender affection will be set ablaze by the fire of ardent desire. No unfamiliar bird can partake of the heat of this Fire, nor can the fowls that dwell upon the dust plunge forth into this heavenly Ocean. However, praise be unto God, ye are the leviathans of this ocean, the birds of this pasture, the moths of this lamp, the nightingales of this meadow.

order.why: Preserve the intense language of burning and illuminating.
shortened: At times, through the outpourings of the Abha Kingdom with spirit and fragrance - O lit candle and O burnt moth! It is the time of burning and melting, that you may illuminate the divine gathering, and the moment of rushing and flying, that you may burn your wings.

order.why: Hear bodily imagery carrying inward attraction.
Connect enkindlement with the Mount Paran image.
shortened: From the cup of the wine of love for the Most Great Name thou hast become intoxicated and enchanted, and from the fire kindled on Mount Paran thou hast been set ablaze and ignited.

order.why: Turn joy outward toward the hearts of others.
shortened: If you were to learn of the glorious gifts of the Abha Kingdom, I swear by the Educator of the seen and unseen that from the intensity of gladness and joy you would blaze out like a ball of fire and ignite the hearts of all horizons, kindle a bright lamp in the glass of contingent being, and freely give your heart and soul in the path of the Beloved.

order.why: Retain the charge to radiate light.
Carry the spark into other lives.
Read the particular address through light upon light.
Connect illumination with service and removal of imaginings.
shortened: The hope from the favors of the Glorious Lord is that you may have a countenance illumined by the lights of the Kingdom, and that in this world of mortality you may become the cause of the spread of heavenly bounties, and in this dusty realm of evanescence you may kindle a luminous lamp and burn away the veils of vain imaginings, and raise high the banner under the Divine Word, and burn and be content with the kindled fire of the Lord.

order.why: Join joy with the work of making hearts steadfast.
shortened: Verily hearts overflow with the wine of attraction, and souls are set ablaze with the fire of enkindlement.
Hearts are gladdened by the appearance of mysteries, and inner consciousness rejoices in the radiance of lights.

But thou - be of good cheer, let thy heart rejoice, and let thy breast be dilated, for thou hast arisen to make hearts steadfast, hast lifted the veils of light, and hast warmed thyself at the fire kindled on the highest Mount.

order.why: Preserve the Christian allusion to a flame surviving opposition.
shortened: They thought that they had done well, that they had extinguished the Lamp, and that they had quenched the Fire which flamed in the tree of Christian certainty; nay, verily, that Lamp hath diffused its dazzling rays unto the Supreme Height and that Fire hath burned until it kindled the hearts of the righteous!"

order.why: Read renewed reflection of love amid affliction.
shortened: This Wronged One is the target of a thousand poisoned arrows at every breath; despite this, the breast becomes a mirror and the lights of the love of God are more brilliantly reflected.

order.why: Keep the candle and overflowing chalice together.
shortened: It is a camphor candle burning and melting, it is a pure chalice overflowing in the gathering of mysteries.
For His grace is magnificent and His sovereignty eternal, His bounty continuous and His throne established, His crown radiant and His lamp guiding the path.

order.why: Turn the imagery into a petition for assistance.
shortened: I entreat Thee, O my God, by Thy name through which the clouds have rained down their rain, and the streams have flowed, and the fire of Thy love hath been enkindled throughout Thy dominion, to assist Thy servant who hath turned towards Thee, and hath spoken forth Thy praise, and determined to help Thee.

order.why: Give illumination an ethical expression in doing good.
shortened: Fix your gaze upon and hold fast to this blessed word which is like a lamp in the darkness of the world. He saith: "Do good even as God hath dealt goodly with thee."

order.why: Read paradise through nearness to divine light.
Encounter the Báb’s paradoxes in their distinct scriptural setting.
shortened: God hath created no being, male or female, save for the fire of the hearts which speaketh laudably around the ocean. As for him who giveth himself in love of the fire and guardeth himself from the fire, he is among the people of Paradise, recorded as being around the fire.
O people of the earth! Hold fast to the cord of God, the Impregnable -- Our Remembrance, this Arabian Youth Who hath been concealed at the point of ice upon seas of fire.

order.why: Preserve the Báb’s numerical and symbolic language without inventing a gloss.
Keep the selected account of divine creation and revealed verses.
shortened: Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the kingdom of the glory of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever lieth between them, and He is the Creator, the Inaccessible.

Say: Even as God hath brought forth these verses from My soul, likewise hath He brought forth the spirits of these verses by the issuing forth of the letters, and they have testified that there is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved. Say: Such is a proof that hath shone forth from the Most Exalted Horizon.

order.why: Read the alternatives concerning elemental fire as metaphysical discussion.
shortened: Some maintain that the source and essence of elemental fire is the warmth in the hearts of lovers and the sighs of yearning souls.

And in the estimation of them that are endowed with divine vision and spiritual insight, the cause of elemental fire and its generation is from the Pen of Destiny which is occupied in inscription, and from it the freedom of all created things hath been and shall be made manifest.

order.why: Retain the analogy between combustion and spiritual attraction.
Keep the reported ignition analogy without adopting it as modern physics.
Close linked passages with love’s drops setting creation ablaze.
shortened: All the atoms of the earth have celebrated Thy praise, and all created things have been set ablaze with the drops sprinkled by the ocean of Thy love, and yet the people still seek to quench Thy fire.

order.why: Read the supplied Báb passage concerning fire within water.
End with the supplied Christian mystic’s conjunction of fire and living water.

questions: How does the meaning of fire change from one passage to another, and what helps you recognize the change?
What do the combinations of fire, light, and water make possible that a single image would not?
How does the distinction between inference, sight, and experience deepen the question of spiritual knowledge?
What does the burning bush in Exodus illuminate, and which meanings belong specifically to the Bahá’í passages?
How do images of attraction and illumination become connected with conduct and service?
What questions arise when you place the Báb’s symbolic language and the supplied Christian mystical passage beside the other readings?

references.label: 1 · Exodus 3:1–6 · The bush that burns without being consumed
references.note: Moses turns aside to investigate a bush burning without being consumed, hears God’s call, and removes his shoes on holy ground. Compare this meeting of wonder, revelation, and reverence with the compilation’s repeated allusions to the Fire and the Mount. The Exodus narrative does not itself identify fire with water; that further transformation belongs to the symbolic work of the passages being studied.
